answer:
Simulate a 2D lid-driven cavity flow using icoFoam.
The cavity is a square of 0.1 m width by 0.1 m height, with a z-thickness of 0.01 m.
The mesh is a uniform Cartesian grid of 20 cells in x and 20 cells in y.
The blockMeshDict vertices are (0 0 0), (0.1 0 0), (0.1 0.1 0), (0 0.1 0), extruded 0.01 m in z.
The domain has three patches: movingWall (top, y=0.1), fixedWalls (left, right, bottom), and frontAndBack (z-faces).
The fluid is incompressible with kinematic viscosity nu = 0.001 m²/s, set in constant/transportProperties.
The top wall (movingWall) has a fixedValue velocity of (1 0 0) m/s.
The fixedWalls have a noSlip velocity boundary condition.
The frontAndBack patch has an empty velocity boundary condition.
The initial velocity field U is (0 0 0) throughout the domain.
The pressure boundary conditions are zeroGradient on movingWall and fixedWalls, and empty on frontAndBack.
No fixedValue pressure reference point or refCell is applied.
The initial pressure field p is 0 throughout the domain.
Time controls: startTime = 0, endTime = 0.5 s, deltaT = 0.002 s, writeControl = timeStep, writeInterval = 20.
The total number of time steps is 250, with results written every 20 steps.
system/fvSchemes uses the default icoFoam template settings.
system/fvSolution uses the default icoFoam template settings.
